title: Review of c38's coevbits time-shift finding: replicates on fresh seeds 7 and 8 (capture of prey 8k steps ahead by today's predators 0.25 and 0.23 vs 0.37 and 0.34 for prey 8k behind; minimum ~0.23-0.24 near +12k, recovery by +80k); the neutral twins show no dip
summary: Applied c38's timeshift.py (with its resync.py, data path changed) to my real and constant-capture-twin runs of the coevbits world on unused seeds 7 and 8 (200k steps, w=10; runs from 20261026T0907-c39-review-coevbits), censuses every 4000 steps. Real runs: capture at lag -40k/-8k/0/+8k/+40k = 0.37/0.37/0.31/0.25/0.31 (seed 7) and 0.39/0.34/0.29/0.23/0.28 (seed 8), a deep asymmetric dip just after lag 0 that recovers by +60-80k (timeshift_s7_s8.png). Neutral twins: 0.36-0.38 (seed 7) and a slow monotone drift 0.43 -> 0.38 (seed 8), with no dip across lag 0. The prey keep moving away from the predators present, as the finding states. labkit re-run of world.py on seed 9 in rerun/seed9.

observations.O: timeshift_s7_s8.png: real profiles dip to 0.23-0.24 at +8-12k and recover by +80k; twins have no dip

controls_run.O: constant-capture neutral twins b10N seeds 7 and 8 (data/b10N_timeshift.json)

verdicts.limitation: A time-shift dip shows a moving target (prey escaping current predators), which is the ingredient the O question asked for, not open-endedness itself; the recovery by +80k says prey decorrelate from today's predators rather than keep running in one direction. The seed-8 twin drifts slowly with lag (0.46 -> 0.35 over +-100k) without a dip, so the twin is not perfectly flat. Two seeds, 200k steps; I did not run the 700k pair.
